messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the melting/freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  
This follows the water phase diagram: as pressure falls below atmospheric levels, the solid–liquid equilibrium line shifts to lower temperatures, giving a freezing point of about –2 °C at 10 kPa.
